summary:
Andorra's legal framework for trans people rests on the 2022 Law of the Person and Family, which introduced legal gender recognition provisions alongside unified civil marriage. Anti-discrimination protection on grounds of gender identity is comparatively recent and narrower than the coverage in neighbouring Spain, and the hate-crime provision is drafted generically rather than naming sexual orientation or gender identity.

Police recorded an average of two to three bias-motivated incidents per month during 2025. DiversAnd, the country's principal LGBTI organisation, flagged incidents around the June Pride celebrations and called for a formal system to register and classify bias-motivated violence so that such acts can be recognised as hate crime; the sources document no such system in operation. The Ministry of Equality implemented equality measures during the same year.

Gender-affirming care for young people remains a matter of advocacy rather than settled provision. In August 2023 DiversAnd met the Ministry of Health to press for protocols covering puberty blockers and hormone therapy for 16-year-olds, and in some cases 14-year-olds, following the 2022 regulatory changes. A transphobic opinion piece published in El Periòdic d'Andorra on 27 September 2023 was removed online with a public apology after DiversAnd objected, although the article had already run in print.

For the visitor, no facility or bathroom law restricts trans people, and no document-gender checks are applied at the open land border with Spain and France; Andorra lies outside the Schengen area. Social tolerance is high in practice despite a conservative Catholic history, and the Ministry of Equality requires companies to maintain sexual and gender-based harassment protocols.
tangentialFactors:
Andorra's head of government, Xavier Espot Zamora, has held office since 2019 and came out as gay publicly in September 2023, stating that he had never hidden it. A serving head of government living openly is a signal about the surrounding social climate rather than a trans-specific legal guarantee.

The country's small population and dependence on tourism shape how the evidence should be read: absolute incident counts stay low, and the documentary base for trans-specific questions is correspondingly thin. The shallower gender-identity coverage compared with Spain is a difference of degree within an otherwise aligned legal tradition, not a divergence into hostility.

The removal of a transphobic newspaper column after an NGO complaint shows that corrective pressure from civil society can work on local media, though it does not operate as a legal remedy.
localsOnly:
The age of consent is 16 under Article 206 of the Penal Code. GayLawNet's Andorra page indexes civil unions, discrimination, hate crimes, marriage, sodomy and trans legal status as areas covered by domestic law.

Residents can enter a civil union as well as a marriage, and can rely on the discrimination and hate-crime provisions, subject to the generic drafting of the latter. Companies are required to keep sexual and gender-based harassment protocols, an obligation administered by the Ministry of Equality, which also implemented equality measures during 2025.

Advocacy routes are open and used: DiversAnd has met the Ministry of Health directly over gender-affirming protocols for minors, has secured the removal and apology for a transphobic newspaper article, and has pressed the authorities to register and classify bias-motivated violence.
outOfScopeNotes:
GayLawNet's Andorra page carries a 'limited information' marking and indexes legal topics without reproducing statutory text; the age of consent and the indexed provisions were not verified against primary sources in this pass.

Whether the Ministry of Health has since adopted the gender-affirming protocols requested by DiversAnd in August 2023, and what the 2022 regulatory changes provide in practice for 14- and 16-year-olds, is unresolved in the sources.

Whether a formal system to register and classify bias-motivated violence has been established following DiversAnd's call is unresolved. The monthly incident figures reported by police are not broken down by protected characteristic, so the trans-specific share of those incidents is unresolved.

Implementation detail for the legal gender recognition provisions of the 2022 Law of the Person and Family, including processing times and any medical requirements, is not sourced here.
